claim: One shared content-egress policy governs both the live-mirror hook and the Rust digest path; redaction happens before egress on both; the three outcome states are distinguishable under network denial; and a mirrored provenance reference survives buffer eviction and restart.

implemented.policy_document: config/egress-policy.json — enumerates content, recipients, providers, encryption, transport and log retention PER PATH, plus the switch table, the four invariants and the outcome vocabulary.
implemented.shared_off_switch: AGENTBOX_EGRESS=0 disables EVERY path. The review's finding was that AGENTBOX_LIVE_MIRROR=0 said nothing about the separately configured Rust digest path; both now obey one global switch as well as their own.
implemented.redaction_before_egress: config/hooks/lib/egress-policy.cjs (JS) and services/nostr-pod-bridge/src/egress_policy.rs (Rust) implement the same rules. The live hook redacts BEFORE composition and before the NIP-59 wrap; the digest path redacts BEFORE the provider request is built, because curating the provider's output does not undo its receipt of the input.
implemented.cross_language_parity: tests/fixtures/egress-redaction.v1.json is a PAIRED fixture both implementations must satisfy exactly. The Rust test reads the same file, so a divergence fails cargo test rather than being noticed later.
implemented.fail_closed: A redaction failure is a SKIP. AGENTBOX_EGRESS_REDACTION=0 disables the PATH rather than sending unredacted content — there is no configuration that sends raw text.
implemented.recipients: Grammar (64 lowercase hex) plus an optional enumerated allowlist (AGENTBOX_MIRROR_RECIPIENTS). The review noted syntax was checked but no allowlist existed.
implemented.outcomes: skipped / attempted / accepted / failed are emitted by both paths. publishWrap() previously resolved with nothing on relay-OK, rejection, socket error, close and timeout alike — the mechanical reason exit zero could not prove delivery. It now returns which outcome occurred.
implemented.log_retention: The mirror dry run prints the REDACTED body, so diagnostics can never retain more than the wire.
implemented.provenance_durability: management-api/utils/agent-event-archive.js — a bounded, rotating, fail-open JSONL archive the publisher appends to before eviction can occur. The resolver falls back to it and returns the FULL ORDERED HISTORY for a reference rather than the newest match, reporting `source` and `history_complete`. A bare numeric event id is labelled process-local and deliberately NOT resolved against the archive, because ids restart at 1 in a new process.

tests.network_denial: The mirror is pointed at ws://127.0.0.1:1 (the discard port), so nothing can leave the machine. Asserted: a denied relay yields ATTEMPTED then FAILED and never ACCEPTED; a disabled path never reaches ATTEMPTED; exit zero holds in all three cases and proves nothing.
tests.redaction_evidence: An invented `password=hunter2 token=abc123` prompt produces a composed body containing neither value, on both the child-key and explicit-recipient configurations; an invented 64-hex nsec becomes <redacted-hex>.
tests.provenance_evidence: After the ring buffer genuinely evicts a reference (asserted as a precondition, 1,005 unrelated events), the reference still resolves from the archive. Three decisions under one session reference return in order. An empty in-memory buffer with the archive intact — the restart case — still resolves.

remaining: No real transcript, provider call or relay send was exercised; the digest path's provider hop is source-verified and unit-tested, not run.
The resolver has no caller or resource authorisation of its own, so an authorised mobile journey from decryption through lookup to the original evidence is still not demonstrated.
The archive is a provenance record, not a database: retention is bounded by rotation, and an expired record is reported as absent-with-a-reason rather than recoverable.
Relay/read policy for the signed kind-30840 digest remains a separate boundary.
